facts: The oracle for this feature already exists and was authored before the implementation: test/integration/pool-lifecycle.integration.spec.ts implements TCON-POOL-0001/0002/0003 against INV-POOL-2 and INV-POOL-4. Do not re-author it and do not write a second oracle for the same conditions.

The implementation this oracle judges is complete and approved: feat-workspace-pool is done, src/workspace/workspace-pool.ts is sha256 a72b2ed5afff75691465ad044b5d49c07056fb40548fd3e1e7fdf4a2430d12a8, and its own verification (10 unit + 2 integration tests) was independently replayed green by the checker on 2026-08-22 under five mutants. Start from 'the pool is probably right', not from 'the pool is probably wrong'.

ESTABLISHED DEFECT, do not rediagnose: TCON-POOL-0003 is currently RED because of the ORACLE, not the implementation. Inside the per-acquire loop the test iterates the whole of recorder.stopOrder and asserts each of those projects is absent from pool.status(). Its own fixture sequence is [p0, p1, p0, p2, p0], which re-acquires p0 after p0 was evicted, so p0 is correctly live again and the absence assertion fires on a workspace that was legitimately restarted.

TCON-POOL-0003's validated condition text is the authority and it does not require permanent absence: it scopes status-absence to the observation moment ('immediately after each eviction -- observed via pool.status() no longer listing that workspace -- the evicted workspace's absolute -data directory still exists'). The oracle over-asserts beyond its own condition. The condition file itself needs no redesign, so no test-designer turn is required for this fix.

PRE-AUTHORISED CORRECTION, exactly one, recorded in harness/DECISIONS.md (2026-08-22): scope the status-absence assertion to workspaces that were evicted AND have not since been re-acquired. Everything else in that file stays byte-identical — the fixture sequence, the cap-1 recorder, the LRU model in TCON-POOL-0002, and the closing assertion that the same workspace was evicted at least twice.

HARD BOUND on that correction: the -data directory existence check must remain unconditional for every project that ever appears in recorder.stopOrder. That assertion IS the INV-POOL-4 falsifier ('an evicted workspace's -data directory is deleted instead of kept for warm restart'). Narrowing, skipping or try/catching it turns a green run into a false pass and the checker will reject the feature.

The rest of this oracle was independently confirmed to have falsifying power, so a green run after the correction is meaningful: under a mutant that suffixes dataDir with a per-call tick, TCON-POOL-0003 fails on 'a re-requested workspace must reuse its warm -data directory' — INV-POOL-4 warm restart is genuinely pinned. Under a mutant making terminate() a no-op, the pool's own integration oracle goes red.

Evidence expectations for this feature: the recorded red (2026-08-20, 3 failures, module absent) is stale — it predates the implementation. Record a fresh red run showing TCON-POOL-0003 failing on the over-broad absence assertion, then the green run after the correction. A green-only evidence list is reported as evidence-no-red by verify-harness.mjs.

Scope fence: the router/pool workspace-identity agreement gap is NOT this feature's problem. It is cut as feat-prove-workspace-identity with its own oracle file. Do not widen this oracle, its conditions, or its falsifier to reach across to project-router.
